why: I checked every verifier PASS/FAIL condition against its line. None is stricter than the line. Check 1 asks only for the `<path>:N:` prefix followed by some error text, not exact wording. Its two-bad-rows probe follows from "every row". Check 2 asks for any non-empty stderr and exit 2. Check 3 checks the shape of `[{ line, error }]`. Check 4 requires only the fields the line lists, plus test coverage. Check 6 has no branch-name rule and no limit on which files the PR may touch. The mutation test, the shebang check and the CRLF check sit under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)", so they don't count as conditions. Every behaviour line is checked by running the program: Checks 1 and 2 run the bin on temp files, Check 3 imports and calls `lint`, and Checks 4 and 6 run npm test. Only Check 5 relies on file reads and grep, and its line is about files existing. The builder brief contains no checks.
